Munich massacre: 1972 Summer Olympics terrorist attack. The militants infiltrated the Olympic Village, killed two members of the Israeli Olympic team, and took nine other Israeli team members hostage.
Emerging in the 1970s among disillusioned liberal hawks, this political movement peaked in influence under George W. Bush and helped drive the push to invade Iraq in 2003 — what is it called?
Neoconservatism: Political movement of former liberals that combines political and social conservatism.
A Peronist who governed Argentina from 2003 to 2007, he later became the country's first 'first gentleman' when his wife succeeded him as president — who was he?

Néstor Kirchner: President of Argentina from 2003 to 2007. Néstor Carlos Kirchner Ostoić (25 February 1950 – 27 October 2010) was an Argentine lawyer and politician who served as the president of Argentina from 2003 to 2007.

One of the Three Kingdoms of Korea alongside Goguryeo and Silla, this kingdom in the southwest had the largest population of the three and was founded by Onjo near present-day Seoul. Which kingdom was it?
Paekche: Ancient Korean kingdom (18 BCE – 660 CE)
Considered the most influential artist of the Flemish Baroque, this painter and diplomat was known for dramatic, sensual compositions and designs for tapestry workshops — who is he?
Peter Paul Rubens: Flemish artist and diplomat (1577–1640)

Held every June in many cities to commemorate the 1969 Stonewall riots, this annual LGBTQ celebration of rights and self-acceptance began as marches in Chicago, New York, LA, and San Francisco in 1970 — what's it called?
Pride parade: LGBTQ celebration event. The events sometimes also serve as demonstrations for legal rights such as same-sex marriage.
Third pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty, he waged 15 military campaigns and reigned 66 years — the longest recorded of any pharaoh — earning the title 'the Great.' Who was he?
Ramesses II: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1279 to 1213 BC.
An Italian neurobiologist who shared the 1986 Nobel for discovering nerve growth factor and served as a senator for life, she became the first Nobel laureate to turn 100 — who is she?

Serving as Ukraine's Defence Minister from 2023 to 2025 before becoming Secretary of the National Security and Defence Council, this Crimean Tatar politician has co-chaired a Crimea diplomatic initiative since 2020 — who is he?
The youngest person ever to hold the office, this Filipino politician became her country's vice president after serving multiple terms as mayor of Davao City — who is she?
Sara Duterte: Vice President of the Philippines since 2022.
The son of Ramesses I and father of Ramesses the Great, this Nineteenth Dynasty pharaoh ruled Egypt from around 1290 to 1279 BC — who was he?
Seti I: Egyptian pharaoh. Menmaatre Seti I (or Sethos I in Greek) was the second pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty of Egypt during the New Kingdom period, ruling 1290 BC to 1279 BC.
Deported to Auschwitz as a teenager, she later championed France's 1975 law legalizing abortion and became the first woman to lead the European Parliament. Who was she?
A onetime Socialist who became a Macron advisor and helped launch En Marche!, this French politician later served briefly as Foreign Minister before joining the European Commission — who is he?
Stéphane Séjourné: French lawyer and politician (born 1985)
This Japanese politician served as Prime Minister from 2008 to 2009 and later became the longest-serving Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister in the country's history — who is he?
Tarō Asō: Prime Minister of Japan from 2008 to 2009. Tarō Asō (麻生 太郎, Asō Tarō; born 20 September 1940) is a Japanese politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 2008 to 2009.

Blaming rich families' land-grabbing for a supposed decline in Rome's population, this politician pushed an agrarian reform law to shift land to poorer citizens — and was killed for it in 133 BC. Who was he?
Tiberius Gracchus: Roman politician and social reformer (163 – 133 BC)

Known as the Risorgimento, this 19th-century movement folded numerous peninsular states into the Kingdom of Sardinia in 1861 and finished in 1871 when Rome became the new nation's capital — what was it?
Unification of Italy: 1848–1870 consolidation of Italian states.
This former heavyweight boxer holds a PhD and has served as the mayor of Kyiv since 2014 — who is he?
Vitali Klitschko: Ukrainian politician and boxer (born 1971)
Founded, by legend, by Cerdic and Cynric of the Gewisse, this Anglo-Saxon kingdom in southern Britain lasted from around 519 to 927 — what was it called?
Wessex: Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the south of Great Britain.
Son of Darius the Great and a grandson of Cyrus the Great, this Achaemenid King of Kings is best remembered for his doomed 480 BC invasion of Greece — who?
Xerxes I: King of Kings of the Achaemenid Empire from 486 to 465 BC.
Nicknamed the 'Young Marshal' after his father's assassination, this Chinese general arrested Chiang Kai-shek in 1936 to force a united front against Japan — who is he?
Zhang Xueliang: Chinese general and warlord (1901–2001)
Who among these was born first?
Soichiro Honda (born 1906) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?

Stephen Gray (scientist) (born 1666) is the earliest of the four. Stephen Gray (December 1666 – February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four came first?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
David L. Hill is a physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Ellen Swallow Richards is a chemist. Richards graduated from Westford Academy (second oldest secondary school in Massachusetts) in 1862.
What is the atomic number of Nihonium?
Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
What is the atomic number of Strontium?
Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.
In what year was Jensen Huang born?
Jensen Huang: The son of Taiwanese immigrants, Huang spent his childhood in Taiwan and Thailand before moving to the United States, where he was a student in Kentucky and Oregon.
In what year was Thomas Sowell born?
Thomas Sowell ( SOHL; born June 30, 1930) is an American economist, economic historian, and social theorist.
In what year was Adam Smith born?
Adam Smith: The work is notable for its contribution to economic theory, particularly in its exposition of the concept of absolute advantage.
In what year did Thomas Hobbes die?
Thomas Hobbes: Hobbes's academic journey began in Westport, leading him to the University of Oxford, where he was exposed to classical literature and mathematics.
In what year did Albert Einstein die?
Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 – 18 April 1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist best known for developing the known theory of relativity.
In what year was Chlorine discovered?
Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
Mikoyan MiG-35: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. Marketed as a 4++ generation jet fighter, it is a further development of the MiG-29M/M2 and MiG-29K/KUB fighters.
Which country is HAL Tejas from?
HAL Tejas: India. The aircraft made its first flight in 2001 and entered into service with the IAF in 2015.
Who is credited with discovering Apus?
Apus: Petrus Plancius. Apus is a small constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Cat's Eye Nebula?
Cat's Eye Nebula: William Herschel. It is a well-studied object that has been observed from radio to X-ray wavelengths.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen?
Hydrogen: Henry Cavendish. Hydrogen is a chemical element; it has the symbol H and atomic number 1.
Who is credited with discovering Astatine?
Astatine: Emilio G. Segrè. Astatine is a chemical element; it has symbol At and atomic number 85.

While working at a Soviet computing centre in 1985, this engineer created one of history's most popular video games — yet earned no royalties from it until founding a company with Henk Rogers in 1996. Who is he?
Alexey Pajitnov (born April 16, 1955) is a Russian and American computer engineer and video game designer.
Multicellular, oxygen-breathing, and all descended from a single common ancestor, this kingdom ranges in size from 8.5 micrometers to 33.6 meters. What is it?
Animal are multicellular, eukaryotic organisms belonging to the biological kingdom Animalia.

This English science fiction writer, futurist, and undersea explorer received the 1961 Kalinga Prize, a UNESCO award for popularizing science, across a career spanning novels, essays, and television hosting — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke (16 December 1917 - 19 March 2008) was an English science fiction writer, science writer, futurist, inventor, undersea explorer, and television series host.
Found in almost every habitat except the open sea and the poles, the order Coleoptera is the largest of all and accounts for about a quarter of every known animal species — which insects are these?
Beetle are insects that form the order Coleoptera, in the superorder Holometabola.
Ranging from southern Canada down to Oaxaca, Mexico, this North American wild cat sports black bars on its forelegs and a short, bobbed tail. What animal is it?
Bobcat (Lynx rufus), also known as the wildcat, bay lynx, or red lynx, is one of the four extant species within the medium-sized wild cat genus Lynx.
Located between the lower back and the perineum, these two rounded regions of human anatomy are built around the gluteus maximus — the largest muscle in the human body — name this body part?
Buttocks (sing.: buttock) are two rounded portions of the exterior anatomy of humans, located on the posterior of the pelvic region.
This root vegetable owes its typical orange color to beta-carotene, though heirloom varieties can be white, purple, or even black — what vegetable is it?
Originating in Northern China, this spitz-type dog breed is known for a dense double coat that forms a distinctive ruff around the neck — name the breed?
Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China.
Though it resembles a barn swallow, this medium-sized bird is actually more closely related to hummingbirds than to any swallow, its resemblance being pure convergent evolution — what bird is it?

Common swift (Apus apus) is a medium-sized bird, superficially similar to the barn swallow or house martin but somewhat larger, though not stemming from those passerine species, being in the order Apodiformes.
This transdisciplinary field studies circular causal processes like feedback and recursion, where an action's outcome becomes the input for the next — what field is it?
Cybernetics is the transdisciplinary study of circular causal processes such as feedback and recursion, where the outcomes of actions return as inputs for subsequent actions.

This gut ailment flares up when small pouches in the wall of the large intestine become inflamed, often striking with sudden lower-abdominal pain — fever or bloody stool warns of a complication; what is it?
Diverticulitis is a gastrointestinal disease characterized by inflammation of abnormal pouches - diverticula - that can develop in the wall of the large intestine.
Working with George de Hevesy, this Hungarian chemist theorized that diffusion speed depends on a nuclide's mass and became the world's go-to expert at preparing polonium — who was she?
Elizabeth Rona (20 March 1890 - 27 July 1981) was a Hungarian nuclear chemist, known for her work with radioactive isotopes.

The telltale earth mounds this tunneling mammal pushes to the surface come from its constantly expanding burrow system, and it feeds mainly on earthworms paralyzed by toxins in its saliva — what animal is it?
European mole (Talpa europaea) is a mammal of the order Eulipotyphla.
This Caltech chemical engineer won the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for using 'directed evolution' to engineer enzymes, and later joined Alphabet's board — who is she?
Frances Arnold (born July 25, 1956) is an American chemical engineer and Nobel Laureate.
The last living species in an order that first appeared over 290 million years ago, this disease-resistant "living fossil" with fan-shaped leaves is also called the maidenhair tree — which is it?
Ginkgo biloba (-goh), also known as the maidenhair tree, and often misspelled "gingko" (see Etymology below) is a species of gymnosperm tree native to East Asia.

Rooted in a Hebrew word meaning 'to walk' or 'to go,' this collective body of Jewish religious law guides both worship and everyday life, tracing back to biblical commandments and later rabbinic codes — what is it?
Halakha (hah-), is the collective body of Jewish religious laws that are derived from the Written and Oral Torah.
Before founding his own Italian supercar company, this Argentine-Italian engineer worked for both Renault and Lamborghini — who is he?
Horacio Pagani (auto executive) (born 10 November 1955) is an Argentine-Italian businessman and automobile engineer in the automotive industry.
Its partial form is called 'subileus' — this condition describes an intestine that can't propel its contents forward, whether from a lack of peristalsis or a mechanical blockage — what is it?
Ileus is a disruption of the normal propulsive ability of the intestine.
Most of the flowers used by the global perfume industry for this fragrant genus of shrubs and vines are grown in a single Egyptian village. What plant is it?
Jasmine (botanical name: Jasminum) is a genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family of Oleaceae.

This childhood illness of unknown cause mainly affects kids under five, causing a prolonged fever lasting more than five days that doesn't respond to typical fever-reducing medicine, plus inflamed blood vessels throughout the body — name the syndrome?
Kawasaki disease (also known as mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome) is a syndrome of unknown cause that results in a fever and mainly affects children under 5 years of age.
Named for the German city where it was bred in the mid-19th century, this is a large German dog breed — which breed?
Leonberger is a German breed of large dog. The breed name derives from that of the city of Leonberg, in Baden-Württemberg, where it was bred in the mid-nineteenth century.
Reclassified in 2021 as part of the order Psocodea alongside booklice and barklice, these tiny wingless parasites cement their eggs to a single host for life — what are they called?
Louse (pl.: lice) is the common name for any member of the infraorder Phthiraptera, which contains nearly 5,000 species of wingless parasitic insects.
Google's employee No. 20 and its first woman software engineer, she later left to run a famous internet company as CEO from 2012 until Verizon bought it — who is she?
Marissa Mayer (born May 30, 1975) is an American business executive, software engineer, and investor who served as president and chief executive officer of Yahoo!
This medical condition is diagnosed when the erect length of the affected organ measures at least two and a half standard deviations below the average size for age — what condition is it?
Micropenis is an unusually small penis.
Named for the strong odor males emit during rut to attract mates, this thick-coated Arctic hoofed mammal is called 'the bearded one' in Inuktitut — what's the species?
Muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae.
A highly corrosive mineral compound with the formula HNO3, this strong inorganic acid is colorless but yellows over time as it decomposes. What is this acid?
Nitric acid is an inorganic compound with the formula HNO3. The compound is colorless, but samples tend to acquire a yellow cast over time due to decomposition into oxides of nitrogen.
Known for causing bones that fracture easily, this group of genetic disorders can also produce blue-tinted eye whites, short stature, and hearing loss. Name the condition?
Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI), colloquially known as brittle bone disease, is a group of genetic disorders that all result in bones that break easily.
Innervated by two dedicated nerves and inserting near the upper arm's bicipital groove, which broad chest muscle flexes and internally rotates the humerus?
Pectoralis major (from Latin pectus 'breast') is a thick, fan-shaped or triangular convergent muscle of the human chest.

This eating disorder involves compulsively craving or eating substances not meant for consumption, and takes its name from the Latin word for a magpie famed in folklore for eating anything — what is it?
Pica (disorder) is the psychologically compulsive craving or consumption of objects that are not normally intended to be consumed.
Which compound pulls double duty as a dietary iodine supplement and as the pill that protects the thyroid gland during radiation emergencies?
Potassium iodide (KI) is a chemical compound, medication, and dietary supplement.
This collective name covers several genera of mid-sized game birds, split between Old World and New World families despite their similar appearance — what birds are they?
Quail is a collective name for several genera of mid-sized birds generally placed in the order Galliformes.
With a surface temperature over 12,000 Kelvin and a radius more than seventy times the Sun's, this blue supergiant is the brightest point of light in Orion — which star?
Rigel is a blue supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion.
Marked by hearing voices, disorganized thinking, and flat affect, this condition is diagnosed by observed behavior rather than any objective test — what is it?
Schizophrenia is a mental disorder characterized variously by hallucinations (typically, hearing voices), delusions, disorganized thinking or behavior, and flat or inappropriate affect.
This small, wingless, primitive insect takes its name from its silvery grey color and darting, fish-like movements — and its scientific name hints at a diet of sugars and starches. What is it?
Silverfish (Lepisma saccharinum) is a species of small, primitive, wingless insect in the order Zygentoma (formerly Thysanura).
Defined as exactly 101,325 pascals and roughly equal to Earth's average sea-level air pressure, what is this reference unit of pressure called?
Standard atmosphere (unit) (symbol: atm) is a unit of pressure defined as 101325 Pa.
This American singer-songwriter has won eleven Grammy Awards across folk, alternative country, and Americana, and was named one of Time's Women of the Year in 2026. Who is she?
Tagetes is a genus of 50 species of annual or perennial, mostly herbaceous plants in the family Asteraceae.
This genus of roughly 350 species of aromatic Mediterranean herbs is the source of a common culinary seasoning that shares its name — what is the genus?
Thymus (plant) (thymes) contains about 350 species of aromatic perennial herbaceous plants and subshrubs in the family Lamiaceae.

This genus of giant theropod dinosaur, whose best-known species takes a Latin name meaning 'king,' roamed an island continent that is now western North America at the very end of the Cretaceous period — name the genus?

Tyrannosaurus is a genus of large theropod dinosaur. The type species Tyrannosaurus rex (rex meaning 'king' in Latin), often shortened to T. rex or colloquially T-Rex, is one of the best represented theropods.
Named after the Scottish engineer who improved the Newcomen steam engine in 1776, this SI unit of power equals one joule per second — what is it?
Watt (symbol: W) is the unit of power or radiant flux in the International System of Units (SI), equal to 1 joule per second or 1 kgm2s3.

This teenage prodigy's work on solvable polynomials helped birth what's now called group theory, and his fiery Republican politics landed him in prison before a fatal duel ended his life at 20 — who was he?
Évariste Galois (25 October 1811 - 31 May 1832) was a French mathematician and political activist.
Recognizable by its black-and-white striped legs and a lyre-shaped marking on its thorax, this mosquito native to North Africa spreads dengue and yellow fever worldwide — what is it?
Aedes aegypti: Species of mosquito. The mosquito can be recognized by black and white markings on its legs and a marking in the form of a lyre on the upper surface of its thorax.
This German polar researcher proposed in 1912 that the continents were slowly drifting apart, a theory mainstream geology only accepted decades later thanks to palaeomagnetism — who was he?
Alfred Wegener: German climatologist and geophysicist (1880–1930)

Inspired by Ørsted's 1820 discovery that current creates a magnetic field, this principle relating a magnetic field's circulation to the current passing through a loop was later generalized by Maxwell with a displacement current term — which physics principle?
Ampère's circuital law: Concept in classical electromagnetism.

A political economy professor turned finance minister after a 1926 coup, this Portuguese dictator ruled his corporatist 'New State' from 1932 until 1968, in one of modern Europe's longest authoritarian regimes — who is he?
António de Oliveira Salazar: Prime Minister of Portugal from 1932 to 1968.
Also nicknamed the toddy cat or musang, this small viverrid native to South and Southeast Asia is IUCN-listed as least concern yet still poached for the illegal wildlife trade — what is it?
Asian palm civet: Species of mammal.

Native to West and Central Africa, this nonvenomous constrictor is the smallest of its kind on the continent and earns its common name from its habit of curling into a tight coil when frightened — which species?
Ball python: Species of constricting snake.
According to scholar John Carter, this discipline has two senses: a list of works consulted by an author, and the systematic study of books as physical objects — what's it called?
Bibliography: Organized listing of books and the systematic description of them as objects.

A four-engined American heavy bomber from the 1930s, it dropped more tonnage than any other aircraft in World War II and ranks as the third-most produced bomber in history, after the B-24 and German Ju 88—what is this legendary aircraft?

Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress: American heavy bomber aircraft. The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).
Also known as undulant fever or Malta fever, this disease is usually caught by drinking unpasteurized milk from infected animals and tends to persist for life — what is it?

Roughly a third of deaths from this group of over 100 diseases trace to tobacco, alcohol, obesity, poor diet and inactivity, and its malignant tumors are defined by uncontrolled cell growth that can spread — what is it?

Cancer: Group of diseases involving cell growth. Cancer is a group of diseases involving uncontrolled cell growth typically resulting in tumors with the potential to invade or spread to other parts of the body.

This branch of metabolism breaks down large molecules such as proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids into smaller units, releasing energy as cells convert the leftovers into waste like carbon dioxide and urea — what's it called?
Catabolism: Set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units.
Built after a 1962 tech-transfer deal with the Soviets fell short on documentation, this Chinese fighter jet is a reverse-engineered derivative of the MiG-21 — which aircraft?
Chengdu J-7: Chinese version of the Soviet MiG-21.
Patented in 1967, this sympathomimetic drug helps people with asthma and other breathing disorders by acting as a bronchodilator — which substance?
Clenbuterol: Chemical compound which aids breathing.
Declared one of the world's most invasive species in 2000 and named Australia's top pest problem in 2008, which highly adaptable Asian bird thrives in cities?
Common myna: Bird of the family Sturnidae.
Nicknamed the jade plant or money plant, this low-maintenance South African succulent thrives on neglect and barely any water — what's its botanical name?
Crassula ovata: Species of succulent. It is sometimes referred to as the money tree; however, Pachira aquatica also has this nickname.
Designed to replace an earlier delta-wing jet for the French Air Force, this fourth-generation single-engine fighter first flew in March 1978 — which aircraft?
Dassault Mirage 2000: French jet fighter aircraft. Work on what would become the Mirage 2000 originated with the "Delta 1000" project launched in 1972.
In this heart condition, the heart chambers become enlarged and lose their ability to pump blood effectively, with causes ranging from genetics to alcohol and cocaine use — what is it called?
Dilated cardiomyopathy: Condition involving an enlarged, ineffective heart.

First imagined by Olaf Stapledon in his 1937 novel Star Maker and later named for a physicist who explored the idea in 1960, this hypothetical megastructure would encircle a star to harvest its energy — what is it?
Dyson sphere: Hypothetical megastructure around a star. A Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

In this lung disease the walls between the alveoli break down, merging tiny air sacs into enlarged spaces that shrink the surface available for gas exchange and starve the blood of oxygen. Which condition is it?
Emphysema: Chronic lung condition. Emphysema is a condition of the lung marked by abnormal enlargement of the alveoli with loss of pulmonary elasticity.
This Hungarian-American theoretical physicist won the 1963 Nobel for applying fundamental symmetry principles to the atomic nucleus and elementary particles — who was he?
Eugene Wigner: Hungarian-American physicist and mathematician (1902–1995)
Made up mostly of undigested food broken down by gut bacteria, this bodily waste is expelled through the anus and can even be dried for fuel or used as fertilizer — what is it?
Feces: Solid or semisolid remains of undigested food.
Despite the name, these fifty species of rodent can't truly fly — they glide between trees using a furred membrane called a patagium. What are they?
Caused by a loss of blood supply and marked by skin turning red or black, this condition comes in dry, wet, and gas forms — what is it?
Gangrene: Type of tissue death by ischemia.
Named from a Latin word for sword, this genus of cormous flowering plants in the iris family is sometimes called the 'sword lily' and is most diverse in South Africa's Cape region — which genus?
Gladiolus: Genus of perennial flowering plants. It is sometimes called the 'sword lily', but is usually called by its generic name (plural gladioli).
Designed specifically for airborne early warning rather than adapted from an existing airframe, this twin-turboprop carrier plane replaced the piston-engined Tracer for the US Navy — which aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye: Airborne early warning and control aircraft. The Northrop Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.
Spiny like a porcupine but actually a distant cousin of the shrew, this nocturnal little mammal comes in 17 species across Europe, Asia, and Africa — and was introduced to New Zealand; what is it?

Widely credited as the 'father of the Indian nuclear programme,' this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and chaired India's first Atomic Energy Commission — who is it?
Homi J. Bhabha: Indian nuclear physicist (1909–1966)

This neurological disorder involves excessive sleepiness or time spent sleeping, sometimes linked to seasonal affective disorder, and appears under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5 — what is it called?

Hypersomnia: Neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness. It can have many possible causes (such as seasonal affective disorder) and can cause distress and problems with functioning.
More than half of all animal species belong to this one chitinous-shelled group, each member sporting three body parts and three pairs of jointed legs — who are they?
Known as the 'snow monkey' for surviving areas buried in snow half the year, no other primate lives farther north than this species — which one?
Japanese macaque: Species of Old World monkey.
Also called the red date or Chinese date, this buckthorn-family fruit is eaten fresh, dried, or candied — what is it?
Jujube: Species of plant with edible fruit.
This colorless noble gas defined the length of the metre from 1960 to 1983, based on the wavelength of one of its spectral lines — which element?
Krypton: Chemical element with atomic number 36 (Kr)
Spread by rats, dogs and other animals, this bacterial blood infection has an acute, jaundice-causing severe form known as Weil's disease — what's the condition?
Leptospirosis: Blood infection caused by bacteria.
Nicknamed the 'Dragon Lady,' this single-engine American spy plane flew covert missions above 70,000 feet over the Soviet Union, China, and Cuba from the 1950s — what is it?

This German physician and sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, mounting what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — and the Nazis revoked his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?
Native to Southeast Asia, this evergreen tree's leaves are known as kratom, containing alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors — which species?
Mitragyna speciosa: Species of plant. It is under preliminary research for possible antipsychotic and antidepressant properties.
Taking its name from the Latin for 'weasel,' this is the largest family in the suborder Caniformia — gathering otters, badgers, martens, and wolverines under one roof. What is it?
Described by Eric Kandel as the 'epic challenge' of biology, this multidisciplinary field studies the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nervous system — what field is it?
Neuroscience: Scientific study of the nervous system.

Producing a distinctive capped nut and supporting more than 950 species of caterpillar, this keystone hardwood genus ranges across the Northern Hemisphere in some 500 species, some evergreen, some deciduous — what tree is it?
Oak: Tree or shrub in the genus Quercus.
A playful, fish-eating cousin of weasels and badgers, this semiaquatic mammal is known for sliding down natural slides and toying with stones — what is it?
A Scottish biologist-turned-town-planner, he coined the word 'conurbation' and gave us one of the earliest versions of 'think globally, act locally' in social science — who was he?
Patrick Geddes: Scottish scientist and town planner (1854–1932)
This legume's raw seeds contain a toxic compound that must be boiled away before eating, though its unripe green pods are eaten as-is — which species is it?
Named from a Greek word meaning 'wanderers,' these large rounded bodies orbit a star or similar object — our solar system has eight, from Mercury to Neptune. What are they called?
Planet: Large, round non-stellar astronomical object.
Marked by high blood pressure and protein in the urine after 20 weeks of pregnancy, this disorder can progress to seizures if left untreated — what is it called?
This seabird's large, colorful beak fades after breeding season, and its short wings beat up to 400 times a minute to keep it airborne — what bird is it?
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago, this Southeast Asian bird species is the primary wild ancestor of today's chickens — which bird?
Red junglefowl: Species of bird; ancestor of the chicken. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
Nicknamed the 'Bone,' this variable-sweep-wing heavy bomber was dreamed up to fuse the B-58's Mach 2 speed with the B-52's range and payload — which aircraft is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer: American strategic bomber.
This business magnate founded the world's largest retailer by revenue in 1962, was the richest person in America throughout the 1980s, and left behind the country's wealthiest family — who is he?
Rising from general secretary in 1981 to FIFA's eighth president in 1998, this Swiss administrator won re-election four times before being suspended in the 2015 corruption scandal — who is he?
Found from Bangladesh to the Philippines, these nocturnal primates make up the genus Nycticebus and include at least eight recognized species — what are they called?
Slow loris: Genus of primates from Southeast Asia.
The sole living member of its genus, this slender, long-legged antelope of southwest Africa sports a white face, a dark eye-to-mouth stripe, and backward-curving horns on both sexes — what is it?
Springbok: Antelope of southwest and south Africa. The springbok or springbuck (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.
Described as the most economically important oxide of its element, this compound with the formula SO3 is a key precursor to sulfuric acid and to acid rain — what is it?
Sulfur trioxide: Chemical compound. Sulfur trioxide exists in several forms: gaseous monomer, crystalline trimer, and solid polymer.

Named after the mathematician who introduced it in 1715, this infinite sum built from a function's derivatives at a single point becomes a special case named for Colin Maclaurin when centered at zero — what is it?
Taylor series: Mathematical approximation of a function.
In the standard anatomical position, this is the outermost digit of the hand, right next to the index finger — which digit, known in Latin as the pollex?
Thumb: First digit of the hand. When a person is standing in the medical anatomical position (where the palm is facing to the front), the thumb is the outermost digit.
